gate.why_opt_in: needs a nightly toolchain (cargo-fuzz passes -Zsanitizer) and compiles with ASAN; the default fast run has neither

coverage: builds all X3-language fuzz targets once with bounded parallelism (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4)
proves defect detection: known-good fixture stays clean, known-bad crashes with an artifact
integration_hardening: local-ci pins RUSTC to the stable toolchain for every gate; fuzz-gate.sh re-points RUSTC/CARGO at the nightly toolchain by absolute path, otherwise -Zsanitizer is rejected.

local-ci exports CARGO_TARGET_DIR for every gate; fuzz-gate.sh overrides it to target-fuzz so nightly ASAN artifacts cannot contaminate the stable target/ (the repo has been bitten by cross-toolchain target dirs before).
a missing nightly, missing cargo-fuzz, or missing rust target is classified BLOCKED (tool-missing), not FAIL.
a build killed by memory pressure is classified BLOCKED (resource), not FAIL.
known_limitations: First cold build was SIGTERM'd under memory pressure on this box (systemd-oomd active, swap nearly full); the gate now builds once with 4 jobs and reports the kill as BLOCKED rather than a code failure. A cold run on a heavily loaded box may still report BLOCKED.
Opt-in only: it does not run on a normal commit and is not part of the release gate yet.
Only 2 of 98 fuzz targets are covered.
next_actions: Promote the fuzz gate from opt-in to the release/nightly set once a cold run is proven stable.
Extend coverage to the pallet fuzz crates (needs the openssl/pkg-config fix).
